title: Incident ODIN: latency wave from burst-controller rollout — rollback & customer hotpatch
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported sudden increases in TTFT and a ~30-60% drop in tokens/sec affecting both short-chat and mid-length completion workloads across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. The customer reports began at 2026-03-11 09:12 UTC and correlated with a staged rollout of the new 'burst_controller' scheduling heuristic (feature flag fc/burst-controller) intended to improve tail variability during high-concurrency bursts.

Immediate impact: High — three paying customers reported production outages or severe degradation (conversational apps timing out or rate-limiting upstream). On Hosted and Dedicated we observed queueing buildup in multiplexed worker lanes and sustained KV-prefetch backoff for contexts between 256-2048 tokens. On Private installs the agent-side config applied the same conservative backoff which left some customer VM pools in a degraded throughput state.

What we did so far (mitigations):
- 2026-03-11 10:05 UTC: Feature flag rollback to conservative mode for Hosted via control-plane toggle (fc/burst-controller=off). Immediate first-byte latency improved for ~70% of affected requests.
- 2026-03-11 11:20 UTC: Issued canary rollback for Dedicated clusters in eu-west-1 and us-east-1, followed by full rollback at 12:00 UTC.
- 2026-03-11 13:40 UTC: Contacted Private customers with off-by-default agent update; provided a hotpatch binary and instructions to revert to runtime-2.3.6 config. Two customers applied hotpatch same day.
- Applied temporary request-level priority bypass for enterprise tokens to prevent prefetch backoff on premium routes.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: The burst_controller's windowed token-rate estimator aggressively reduced prefetch window size for streams that showed a short-lived burst pattern. In mixed-priority multiplexing this heuristic misattributed upstream transient stalls to persistent congestion and triggered an extended backoff. That backoff cascaded into lower tokens/sec and longer TTFT because KV cache warmups and microbatch formation fell below efficient thresholds. The issue was amplified for models with heterogeneous context-framing (different segment lengths) because the estimator used a single decay constant for all variants.

Telemetry pointers:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/innodb-burst-odin (TTFT/token/sec panels)
- Incident incident-2026-03-odin in PagerDuty
- Quick Telemetry snippet: hosted/region/us-east-1 average tokens/sec down 42% between 09:00-11:00 UTC.

Planned corrective work (next steps):
1) Short-term (hotfix, <72h): publish an explicit hotpatch that disables aggressive decay in burst_controller and adds a safe min_prefetch_window; ship runtime-2.3.8-hotfix and coordinate with Private customers for agent rollout.
2) Medium-term (1-3 weeks): rework estimator to be variant-aware (per-model/per-context-length decay constants), add circuit-breaker to avoid extended backoff across multiplex boundaries, and expand unit/integration tests to simulate multiplexed prefetch semantics.
3) Long-term (quarterly): implement controlled rollout telemetry guardrail: automatic pause of rollout if tokens/sec drops >20% for two consecutive telemetry windows for any paying customer.

Acceptance criteria for hotfix:
- tokens/sec returns within 10% of baseline for 95th percentile of requests within 30 minutes of hotfix application
- No new regressions on tail-latency for low-priority best-effort routes

Customer comms:
- Draft incident summary sent to impacted customers on 2026-03-11 16:30 UTC; follow-ups scheduled per-account with Solutions engineers.

Follow-ups / action items:
- Diego: ship runtime-2.3.8-hotfix PR with conservative controller defaults and min_prefetch_window by 2026-03-13 EOD (PR linked below).
- Maya: coordinate postmortem and publish to Confluence once RCA validated.
- ML infra: prototype variant-aware decay constants and add tests simulating mixed context streams.

Notes: we observed no evidence of kernel misselection or quantization regressions in this incident; the regression maps to scheduler heuristic change only.
